- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__create_file
tools.description:
FILE REFERENCES: to upload a file you can read here, don't type its base64; set base64Content to a file reference, sha256:<64 lowercase hex>:<its absolute path, with / between folders>. The app fills in the file's content once the user approves the call. Call this tool to create or upload a File to Google Drive.

If uploading content, prefer `textContent` for text content. For non-UTF8 contents, use the `base64Content` field and base64 encode the data to set on that field.

Returns a single File object upon successful creation.

The following Google first-party mime types can be created without providing content:

 - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` 
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` 
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` 

Folders can be created by setting the mime type to `application/vnd.google-apps.folder`.

When uploading content, the `contentMimeType` field is required and should match the type of the content being uploaded.

By default, supported content will be converted to Google first-party mime types.

To disable conversions for first-party mime types, set `disableConversionToGoogleType` to true.

Pregenerated file IDs (`pregeneratedId`, obtained from `generate_ids`) are supported for non-Google Workspace files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`). When uploading content with `pregeneratedId`, `disableConversionToGoogleType` must be set to true.

base64Content.description: Optional. The base64 encoded content to upload. It's an error to set this and `textContent`.

content.description: Deprecated: Use `base64Content` or `textContent` instead. The content of the file encoded as base64. The content field should always be base64 encoded regardless of the mime type of the file.

contentMimeType.description: The mime type of the content being uploaded. Required when any type of content is provided.

disableConversionToGoogleType.description: Set to true to retain the passed in content mime type and not convert to a Google type. For example, without this a `text/plain` content mime type will be converted to to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`. Has no effect for types that do not have a Google equivalent.

inheritedPermissionsDisabled.description: Set to true to disable inherited permissions on the created folder, restricting access to only users with direct permissions on the folder.

mimeType.description: Deprecated: DO NOT USE!! Set `contentMimeType` instead.

parentId.description: The parent id of the file.

pregeneratedId.description: Optional. The pregenerated id of the file to create, obtained from the `generate_ids` tool. Supported for binary/blob files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`); not supported for native Google Workspace document types. When uploading content with a pregenerated id, `disableConversionToGoogleType` must be set to true.

textContent.description: Optional. The (UTF-8) text content to upload. It's an error to set this and `base64Content`.

title.description: Required. The title of the file.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__share_file
tools.description:
Call this tool to share a Google Drive file with a user, group, Google Chat space, target audience, or anyone with the link.

Specify the recipient using `emailAddress` (for a user or group), `chatSpaceId` (for a Google Chat space), or `permissionId` (for an organizational target audience or `"anyoneWithLink"`, which can be discovered using `get_audience_recommendations`). When shared via `permissionId`, the response includes `shareableLink` to open the file.

If the recipient already has permission to the file, this tool will update their permission level to match the role in this request only if the new role is higher than their current role, or update the expiration time if `expirationTime` is provided.

chatSpaceId.description: Optional. The ID of the Chat space to share with, in the format `spaces/{space}`. Exactly one of `emailAddress`, `chatSpaceId`, or `permissionId` must be provided.

emailAddress.description: Optional. The email address of the user or group to share with. Exactly one of `emailAddress`, `chatSpaceId`, or `permissionId` must be provided.

expirationTime.description: Optional. The time at which this permission will expire. If not set, the permission does not expire. Expiration times have the following restrictions: * They can only be set on `user` and `group` permissions (including Chat spaces). * The time must be in the future. * The time cannot be more than a year in the future. * For folders, expiration time can only be set when `role` is `reader`. * Expiration time cannot be set on Shared Drive root folders.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to share.

permissionId.description: Optional. The permission ID of a target audience (or `"anyoneWithLink"` for public link sharing) to share with. Exactly one of `emailAddress`, `chatSpaceId`, or `permissionId` must be provided.

role.description: Required. The role to grant. Supported roles (in descending order of access level): * `writer` * `commenter` * `reader`

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__trash_file
tools.description:
Moves a Google Drive file to the user's trash.
It does not permanently delete the file.Returns an empty response upon successful completion.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to trash.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__update_file
tools.description:
Call this tool to update the metadata of, or lock/unlock, a Google Drive file.

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is attempting to update.
For moving files, use `search_files` to identify the destination parent id.
For folders, `folderColorRgb` changes the folder color. It must be an RGB hex string in the format `#RRGGBB` and is snapped to the nearest color in Drive's folder color palette.

description.description: Optional. The updated description of the file. If provided as an empty string, clears the existing description.

downloadRestriction.description: Optional. Restrictions applied to downloading, printing, and copying the file. Only the file's owner (or an organizer in a shared drive) can modify download restrictions. Cannot be set on folders, Google Sites, or Google Forms.

etag.description: Optional. Opaque version token used for optimistic concurrency control (preventing concurrent edit conflicts). If set, the update fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION if the file has been modified since the etag was returned. OMIT this field if you have not previously retrieved the file. Never fabricate or manually format an etag value. ONLY pass the exact, unaltered string previously received in `File.etag` or `Revision.file_etag` from a prior read or write operation.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to update.

folderColorRgb.description: The updated color of the folder, as an RGB hex string in the format `#RRGGBB` (e.g. `#4986e7`). Only applies to folders. The color is snapped to the nearest color in Drive's folder color palette.

inheritedPermissionsDisabled.description: Optional. Whether inherited permissions are disabled on the folder. Set to true to disable inherited permissions (restricting access to only users with direct permissions on the folder), or false to re-enable inherited permissions. Only supported for folders.

parentId.description: The updated parent id of the file. If the file has an existing parent, it will be replaced, resulting in a folder move. If provided, must not be empty.

readOnly.description: Optional. Whether the content of the file is read-only. Setting this to true locks the file to prevent edits, comments, suggestions, and title changes. Setting this to false unlocks a previously locked file.

readOnlyReason.description: Optional. Optional reason for why the file was put into a read-only (locked) state. Can only be set when `readOnly` is set to true.

starred.description: Updates the starred state of the file.

title.description: The updated title of the file. If provided, must not be empty.

writersCanShare.description: Optional. Whether users with only writer permission can modify the file's permissions and share the file.

DownloadRestriction.description: Restrictions applied to downloading, printing, and copying a file.

restrictedReader.description: Optional. Whether download, print, and copy are restricted for readers (viewers) and commenters.

restrictedWriter.description: Optional. Whether download, print, and copy are restricted for writers (editors). If true, download, print, and copy are also restricted for readers and commenters.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-create-pages
tools.description:
Creates one or more Notion pages with the specified properties and content.

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do NOT invent Markdown syntax. Put the page title in properties, not content. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Use a named destination as parent. Otherwise use "creation_mode": "draft" for a durable private page. Do not combine draft mode with parent, or move or share it without direction.

For a meeting note, use create_meeting_note if available, even in a Meetings database, unless the user wants a regular page.

For a database, ALWAYS fetch first. Use its collection:// URL as data_source_id, exact property names, and title property. Never put a database ID in page_id. Outside a database, the only allowed property is the required "title".



For reusable instructions, set "is_skill": true. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do not mark ordinary pages or drafts as skills. Report any "warnings" in the result to the user.

properties.description:
The properties of the new page, which is a JSON map of property names to SQLite values.
For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page and is automatically shown at the top of the page as a large heading.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/[redacted]", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

content.description: The content of the new page, using Notion Markdown. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

template_id.description: The ID of a template to apply to this page. When specified, do not provide 'content' as the template will provide it. Properties can still be set alongside the template. Get template IDs from the <templates> section in the fetch tool results. Template application is asynchronous: the page starts blank and content appears shortly after.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to explicitly set no icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to explicitly set no cover. Omit to leave unchanged.

full_width.description: Set to true for a full-width page, or false for the default width. Omit to use the default. For database pages, overrides the database layout for this page only.

is_skill.description: Set to true only when the user asks for reusable instructions or a repeatable workflow. Do not mark ordinary reference pages, one-time documents, or drafts as skills. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. False has the same effect as omitting the field.

preserve_internal_links.description: Preserve internal Markdown links instead of converting them to native mentions.

creation_mode.description: If the user explicitly names a private or shared destination, omit "creation_mode" and use that parent. Otherwise, use "draft" when the user clearly wants a durable page but has not named a destination. Prefer this explicit draft mode over omitting the parent. Draft mode is server-enforced: it creates a private workspace-level page and cannot be combined with "parent". Create it without first asking where it should live. After creation, tell the user it is private and offer to move it once they name a destination.

parent.description: All pages in one call share this parent. Pass "memory" to save a personal memory; see notion://docs/memory. Otherwise use a page (page_id), database page (database_id), data source (data_source_id), or teamspace root (teamspace_id, from get_teams). Teamspace roots require a user-backed connection and permission to add top-level pages. A database_id cannot be used when the database has more than one data source; fetch it and use the right collection:// URL as data_source_id. If omitted, pages are private at the workspace level. When no destination is named, prefer explicit "creation_mode": "draft" over omitting the parent.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, [redacted]

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, [redacted]

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

teamspace_id.description: The ID of the teamspace in which to create top-level pages (with or without dashes).

allow_async.description: Default to true for page creation. Set to false only when the next step needs the created pages immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. tools.description:
Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, data source, or saved database view) by URL or ID.

Provide a URL or ID in `id`. Make multiple calls for multiple entities.

For pages, use path, verification, edit time, and truncation metadata to assess the source. Treat recency as context, not proof. Report material uncertainty when sources conflict.

Pages use Notion-flavored Markdown. For the complete specification, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool.

Pass a `notion://docs/*` URI as `id` to read that MCP documentation resource.

Databases return data sources in `<data-source url="collection://...">` tags. Fetch the collection:// URL for its schema and use it with update_data_source or query_data_sources. Multi-source databases return more than one data source.

Saved views return filters, sorts, and display settings. To query their rows, use query_data_sources with `mode: "view"`.

A null cover or icon means none; an omitted one means unavailable, not absent. Keep a page's Markdown icon attribute for edit round trips. File URLs expire; re-fetch to refresh them. Uploaded media blocks use stable `notion-file-block://` sources; keep them when editing or copying Markdown. Get download URLs with get_file_download_urls, or set `include_file_urls` to true for a `references` map. Before relying on page content, check `truncated`, `unknown_block_count`, and `unknown_block_ids` for omitted subtrees.

Set `include_discussions` to true for discussion counts, markers, previews, and `discussion://` URLs that correlate with get_comments.

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "memory" to fetch the connected user's About page and memory database in this workspace without creating them. Pass a notion://docs/* URI to read that documentation resource. Also accepts an explicit saved view URL (view://...) from a database response. If a database block ID returns a validation error, use the collection:// URL from that error. Example: <example>notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec</example>.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. Defaults to false. When true, full transcripts are included; when false, a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead.

include_discussions.description: Whether to include discussion/comment indicators in the page output. When true, adds a <page-discussions> summary with discussion count, preview snippets, and discussion:// URLs. Use with the get_comments tool to retrieve full discussion content. Defaults to false.

include_file_urls.description: Whether to return signed download URLs for uploaded files. Defaults to false. When false, page Markdown cites uploaded files by stable notion-file-block:// references and the response has no references map; call get_file_download_urls with the references when you need those files' contents. content.text:
Partly. The Apps Scripts stop running, but plain SQL scripts can't replace all of them. Here's what changes:

**Old flow:** Sheet → Apps Script → API route → `lib/` logic → DB
**New flow:** CSV → loader (the CSV pipeline) → staging tables → transform step → final tables

The transform step can be SQL for some sources but not all:

| Target | Plain SQL works? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `merchant_subscriptions`, `merchant_ads`, `ad_conversions` | **Yes** | Straight `INSERT … SELECT` from staging with casts. Easy. |
| `onboarding_cases` (T-1 sync) | **Hard** | Round-robin assignment to onboarders, create or reopen case, write events, language routing. |
| Callbacks → `wa_messages` | **Hard** | 24h merge, owner lookup, round-robin per team, reopen lost case. |

**Options for the hard ones:**
1. **Reuse the app code (recommended).** A scheduled job reads the staging tables and calls the existing `lib/` functions. The logic is already tested.
2. **Rewrite as MySQL stored procedures.** That means a lot of work and two copies of the same logic.

**Something needs a schedule either way.** A cron (Vercel cron, AWS EventBridge, or the MySQL event scheduler) has to run:
- the transform step after each CSV lands
- the daily jobs the leadgen trigger runs today (rebalance, WhatsApps, DND, win-back)

**⚠️ Check this first:** the app still connects with a **Postgres** driver (`lib/db.ts` uses `postgres`), and all its SQL is Postgres-only (`ON CONFLICT`, `jsonb_to_recordset`, `::date`, advisory locks). If the DB is now MySQL, the "same as Neon" schema covers the tables but not the query syntax. Either:
- the app is being ported to MySQL somewhere else (another branch or repo?), or
- the "AWS DB" is actually Postgres (RDS or Aurora Postgres), not MySQL.

That decides whether the existing logic can be reused as-is. Ask whoever did the migration which engine it is.

Here's what the 3 files in the SMB Daily Tracker do.

## 1. `Code.gs`: Gmail CSV → sheet tabs (6 importers)

Each importer finds the latest unread email from `[redacted]` with a CSV attached, **clears the tab, overwrites it with the CSV**, and marks the email read with a label.

| Function | Email subject | Writes tab | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `importCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] OCL Funnel DoD` | **OCL Funnel** | CSV-Processed |
| `importSubCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] Subscription Raw` | **Sub Raw** | CSV2-Processed |
| `importOCLCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] OCL Funnel T` | **OCL TP** | CSV-Processed-2 |
| `importCancelCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] cancellations` | **Cancellations** | CSV33-Processed |
| `MercFunnelCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] merchant_funnel` | **Merchant_Funnel** (only clears A:Q) | CSV133-Processed |
| `ScorecardCSVFromGmail` | `[Report] scorecard_new` | **Scorecard_New** | CSV303-Processed |

None of these send anything to the DB; they only fill sheet tabs. Their triggers aren't in the code, so they were set by hand in the Triggers UI, and the run times aren't visible from here.

## 2. `subs raw sync.gs`: Sub Raw → Onboarding (DB)

- **Reads:** `Sub Raw`, `AdsRun Raw`, `meta_failed_ads`
- **Sends to:** `PI_COMMERCE_SUB_RAW_SYNC_URL` → `/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync`
- **DB result:** `onboarding_cases`, `onboarding_events`, `customers`
- **Creates tab:** `Onboarding Sync Log`, one audit row per run
- **Trigger:** daily ~9:30 IST
- **Differs from the repo copy:** since 25 Oct 2026, each MID under a Cust ID is sent as its own row (one onboarding case per outlet). The live version is newer.

## 3. `ads live and cancelled sub.gs`: CSM sync (DB)

- **Reads:** `Sub Raw`, `AdsRun Raw`
- **Sends to:** `PI_COMMERCE_CSM_SYNC_URL` → `/api/internal/csm-sync` (start → subs → ads → finish)
- **DB result:** `merchant_subscriptions`, `merchant_ads`, `csm_sync_runs`, then the CSM queues: Ads About to End, Ads Ended, Cancelled/Expired, Onboarding Lost
- **Creates tab:** none
- **Trigger:** daily ~9:30 IST

## Flow

```
DaaS email CSV ──Code.gs──► Sub Raw ─┬─ subs raw sync.gs ───────────► onboarding_cases
                                     └─ ads live & cancelled sub.gs ─► merchant_subscriptions / merchant_ads
          ?? ───────────────► AdsRun Raw, meta_failed_ads (read by both, filled by neither)
DaaS email CSV ──Code.gs──► OCL Funnel, OCL TP, Cancellations, Merchant_Funnel, Scorecard_New (sheet reports only)
```

## What this means

1. **Sub Raw is already a CSV upstream.** The `[Report] Subscription Raw` email from DaaS is the source, so the pipeline can ingest that CSV directly with no sheet in between.
2. **Nothing in this sheet fills AdsRun Raw or meta_failed_ads.** The CSM script mentions an "AdsRun Raw Gmail import (~8:55 AM)", so it's probably another DaaS email handled by a script elsewhere. Next step: find which script or sheet does that import.
3. **The 5 report tabs** (OCL Funnel, OCL TP, Cancellations, Merchant_Funnel, Scorecard_New) never reach the DB today. They only matter if dashboards should be built from the DB.
4. **Tab name mismatch:** the script looks for `meta_failed_ads`, but the tab is `Meta_Failed_Ads`. Check that the sync log shows fail reasons being picked up.

Send the next sheet's scripts when ready.

function CallbackCSVFromGmail() {
  const SEARCH_QUERY = 'from:[redacted] subject:"[Report] callback_request" has:attachment filename:csv is:unread';
  const SHEET_NAME = 'Callbacks';
  const PROCESSED_LABEL = '43CSV-Processed';

  const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  let sheet = ss.getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME);
  if (!sheet) sheet = ss.insertSheet(SHEET_NAME);

  let label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(PROCESSED_LABEL);
  if (!label) label = GmailApp.createLabel(PROCESSED_LABEL);

  const threads = GmailApp.search(SEARCH_QUERY);
  if (threads.length === 0) {
    Logger.log('No new matching emails found.');
    return;
  }

  // Only process the MOST RECENT matching email (today's report)
  const thread = threads[0];
  const messages = thread.getMessages();
  const message = messages[messages.length - 1]; // latest message in thread

  const attachments = message.getAttachments();
  attachments.forEach(att => {
    if (att.getName().toLowerCase().endsWith('.csv')) {
      const rows = Utilities.parseCsv(att.getDataAsString());
      if (rows.length === 0) return;

      // Clear everything, then write header + fresh data
      sheet.clearContents();
      sheet.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, rows[0].length).setValues(rows);
    }
  });

  thread.markRead();
  thread.addLabel(label);

  // Label ALL matching threads so old unprocessed ones don't pile up and get picked next run
  threads.forEach(t => t.addLabel(label));

  Logger.log('Sheet overwritten with latest CSV data.');
}

function syncPaytmCallbacks() {
  const props = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties();
  const url = props.getProperty('PI_COMMERCE_PAYTM_CALLBACK_SYNC_URL');
  const [redacted]
  if (!url || !secret) throw new Error('Set PI_COMMERCE_PAYTM_CALLBACK_SYNC_URL and PI_COMMERCE_SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET in Script Properties');
  const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getSheetByName(PCB_SHEET);
  if (!sheet) throw new Error('Tab "' + PCB_SHEET + '" not found');
  const values = sheet.getDataRange().getDisplayValues();
  const header = values[0].map(h => String(h).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, '_'));
  const fields = ['cust_id', 'id', 'mid', 'business_name', 'phone_number', 'requested_at', 'stage', 'reason', 'subscription_status', 'ad_live_status', 'onboarding_stage', 'route_to'];
  const idx = {};
  fields.forEach(f => { idx[f] = header.indexOf(f); });
  ['id', 'phone_number', 'requested_at', 'subscription_status', 'ad_live_status'].forEach(f => {
    if (idx[f] < 0) throw new Error('Missing header: ' + f);
  });
  const rows = [];
  for (let r = 1; r < values.length; r++) {
    const v = values[r];
    if (!v[idx.id]) continue;
    const row = {};
    fields.forEach(f => { row[f] = idx[f] >= 0 ? v[idx[f]] : ''; });
    rows.push(row);
  }
  let created = 0, merged = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < rows.length; i += PCB_BATCH) {
    const res = UrlFetchApp.fetch(url, {
      method: 'post', contentType: 'application/json', muteHttpExceptions: true,
      headers: { 'x-sub-raw-sync-secret': secret },
      payload: JSON.stringify({ rows: rows.slice(i, i + PCB_BATCH) })
    });
    if (res.getResponseCode() !== 200) throw new Error('Portal said ' + res.getResponseCode() + ': ' + res.getContentText().slice(0, 300));
    const j = JSON.parse(res.getContentText()); created += j.created || 0; merged += j.merged || 0;
  }
  console.log('Paytm callback sync: ' + rows.length + ' rows, new requests ' + created + ', repeats within 24h ' + merged);
}

These two belong to **Merchant Callback Request**.

## 1. `CallbackCSVFromGmail`: Gmail CSV → sheet tab

| | |
|---|---|
| Email | from `[redacted]`, subject `[Report] callback_request` |
| Writes tab | **Callbacks**: cleared and overwritten every run |
| Label | `43CSV-Processed` |
| Trigger | set by hand in the Triggers UI, so the time isn't visible from the code |
| DB | none, sheet only |

## 2. `syncPaytmCallbacks`: Callbacks tab → DB

| | |
|---|---|
| Reads | **Callbacks** tab: 12 columns (`cust_id, id, mid, business_name, phone_number, requested_at, stage, reason, subscription_status, ad_live_status, onboarding_stage, route_to`) |
| Sends to | `PI_COMMERCE_PAYTM_CALLBACK_SYNC_URL` → `/api/internal/paytm-callback-sync` |
| DB result | `wa_messages` (the Req Call Back panes in Sales / Onboarding / CSM) and `paytm_callback_ids` |
| Trigger | every 3 h |
| Creates tab | none |

The live copy matches the repo copy.

## Flow

```
DaaS email "[Report] callback_request" ──CallbackCSVFromGmail──► Callbacks tab
                                            ──syncPaytmCallbacks (3h)──► wa_messages + paytm_callback_ids
```

## What this means

- **The source is already a CSV.** The DaaS `callback_request` report can go straight into the DB pipeline, so both scripts can be dropped.
- **Timing gap:** the sync runs every 3 h, but the email import's schedule is unknown. If the import runs once a day, the other syncs just resend old rows. That's harmless, since each request ID is only handled once.
- **`Sheet1` tab:** it has the raw columns without `cust_id`, `subscription_status`, `ad_live_status`, `route_to`. Neither script writes it, so it's probably a manual or old copy. Ignore it.

**Running list of DaaS email reports so far:**

| Report subject | Tab | Goes to DB? |
|---|---|---|
| `Subscription Raw` | Sub Raw | ✅ onboarding + CSM |
| `callback_request` | Callbacks | ✅ wa_messages |
| `OCL Funnel DoD`, `OCL Funnel T`, `cancellations`, `merchant_funnel`, `scorecard_new` | report tabs | ❌ sheet only |
| ? | AdsRun Raw, Meta_Failed_Ads | ✅ but the importer hasn't been found yet |

Send the next sheet's scripts when ready.

function importOnbCSVFromGmail() {
  const SEARCH_QUERY = 'from:[redacted] subject:"[Report] Onboardings_total" has:attachment filename:csv is:unread';
  const SHEET_NAME = 'Onboardings';
  const PROCESSED_LABEL = 'CSV-Processed-1';

  const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  let sheet = ss.getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME);
  if (!sheet) sheet = ss.insertSheet(SHEET_NAME);

  let label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(PROCESSED_LABEL);
  if (!label) label = GmailApp.createLabel(PROCESSED_LABEL);

  const threads = GmailApp.search(SEARCH_QUERY);
  if (threads.length === 0) {
    Logger.log('No new matching emails found.');
    return;
  }

  // Only process the MOST RECENT matching email (today's report)
  const thread = threads[0];
  const messages = thread.getMessages();
  const message = messages[messages.length - 1]; // latest message in thread

  const attachments = message.getAttachments();
  attachments.forEach(att => {
    if (att.getName().toLowerCase().endsWith('.csv')) {
      const rows = Utilities.parseCsv(att.getDataAsString());
      if (rows.length === 0) return;

      // Drop the CSV header row — sheet already has one from earlier runs
      const dataRows = rows.slice(1);

      // Find the last row that actually has content, then append below it
      const lastRow = sheet.getLastRow();
      const startRow = lastRow < 1 ? 1 : lastRow + 1;

      sheet.getRange(startRow, 1, dataRows.length, dataRows[0].length)
           .setValues(dataRows);
    }
  });

  thread.markRead();
  thread.addLabel(label);

  // Label ALL matching threads so old unprocessed ones don't pile up and get picked next run
  threads.forEach(t => t.addLabel(label));

  Logger.log('Appended new rows to sheet.');
}


function importAdsRunCSVFromGmail() {
  const SEARCH_QUERY = 'from:[redacted] subject:"[Report] Adsrun_mail" has:attachment filename:csv is:unread';
  const SHEET_NAME = 'Ads_Run';
  const PROCESSED_LABEL = 'CSV12-Processed';
  const META_AD_ID_COLUMN = 12; // 1-indexed column with the ID_-prefixed meta_campaign_id value

  const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  let sheet = ss.getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME);
  if (!sheet) sheet = ss.insertSheet(SHEET_NAME);

  let label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(PROCESSED_LABEL);
  if (!label) label = GmailApp.createLabel(PROCESSED_LABEL);

  const threads = GmailApp.search(SEARCH_QUERY);
  if (threads.length === 0) {
    Logger.log('No new matching emails found.');
    return;
  }

  const thread = threads[0];
  const messages = thread.getMessages();
  const message = messages[messages.length - 1];

  const attachments = message.getAttachments();
  attachments.forEach(att => {
    if (att.getName().toLowerCase().endsWith('.csv')) {
      const rows = Utilities.parseCsv(att.getDataAsString());
      if (rows.length === 0) return;

      const numRows = rows.length;
      const numCols = rows[0].length;
      const colIndex = META_AD_ID_COLUMN - 1; // 0-indexed for array access

      // Strip the 'ID_' prefix and force the remaining digits to be treated as text,
      // so Sheets never gets a chance to auto-detect it as a number.
      if (numCols >= META_AD_ID_COLUMN) {
        for (let r = 1; r < numRows; r++) { // start at 1 to skip header
          const val = String(rows[r][colIndex] || '');
          if (val.startsWith('ID_')) {
            rows[r][colIndex] = "'" + val.substring(3); // strip prefix, force text
          }
        }
      }

      sheet.clearContents();

      // Belt-and-suspenders: also pre-set the column format as plain text
      if (numCols >= META_AD_ID_COLUMN) {
        sheet.getRange(1, META_AD_ID_COLUMN, numRows, 1).setNumberFormat('@');
      }

      sheet.getRange(1, 1, numRows, numCols).setValues(rows);
    }
  });

  thread.markRead();
  thread.addLabel(label);
  threads.forEach(t => t.addLabel(label));

  Logger.log('Sheet overwritten with latest CSV data.');
}


/**
 * Incremental import: Superset emails a CSV containing only recent ads.
 * - Ads already in the sheet (matched on Ad_ID) are overwritten in place.
 * - New Ad_IDs are appended at the bottom.
 * - Columns are found by header name, so column order changes don't break it.
 */

const CFG = {
  SEARCH_QUERY: 'from:[redacted] subject:"[Report] Onb_Ads_New" has:attachment filename:csv is:unread',
  SHEET_NAME: 'New',
  PROCESSED_LABEL: 'CSV225-Processed',
  KEY_HEADER: 'Ad_ID',
  // Columns that must stay text (long IDs lose digits if Sheets turns them into numbers)
  TEXT_HEADERS: ['PhoneNo', 'Meta_Campaign_ID', 'Ad_Account_ID', 'Meta_AD_ID'],
  // Column whose values arrive as 'ID_123...' and need the prefix removed
  PREFIXED_HEADER: 'Meta_AD_ID',
  PREFIX: 'ID_'
};

/** Daily trigger: run this one. */
function importNewAdsCSVFromGmail() {
  const sheet = getSheet_();
  const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(CFG.PROCESSED_LABEL) || GmailApp.createLabel(CFG.PROCESSED_LABEL);

  const threads = GmailApp.search(CFG.SEARCH_QUERY);
  if (threads.length === 0) {
    Logger.log('No new matching emails found.');
    return;
  }

  // Oldest first, so if a day was missed the newer file is applied last and wins.
  threads.reverse().forEach(thread => {
    const msgs = thread.getMessages();
    const msg = msgs[msgs.length - 1];
    const att = msg.getAttachments().find(a => a.getName().toLowerCase().endsWith('.csv'));
    if (!att) return;

    const rows = Utilities.parseCsv(att.getDataAsString());
    const result = upsertRows_(sheet, rows);
    Logger.log('%s -> updated %s, appended %s', att.getName(), result.updated, result.appended);

    // Only mark as processed after a successful write, so a failure is retried next run.
    thread.markRead();
    thread.addLabel(label);
  });
}

/**
 * ONE-TIME full load. The full file is too big to email (SES 10 MB limit).
 * 1. Run the original (unfiltered) query in SQL Lab, download the CSV.
 * 2. Upload it to Google Drive and put its exact file name below.
 * 3. Run this function once from the editor. It REPLACES the whole sheet.
 */
function initialLoadFromDrive() {
  const FILE_NAME = 'Onb_Ads_New.csv';
  const files = DriveApp.getFilesByName(FILE_NAME);
  if (!files.hasNext()) throw new Error('File not found in Drive: ' + FILE_NAME);
  const rows = Utilities.parseCsv(files.next().getBlob().getDataAsString());

  const sheet = getSheet_();
  sheet.clearContents();
  upsertRows_(sheet, rows);
  Logger.log('Full load done: %s data rows', rows.length - 1);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function getSheet_() {
  const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  return ss.getSheetByName(CFG.SHEET_NAME) || ss.insertSheet(CFG.SHEET_NAME);
}

function upsertRows_(sheet, rows) {
  if (!rows.length) return { updated: 0, appended: 0 };

  const header = rows[0].map(h => String(h).replace(/^/, '').trim());
  const numCols = header.length;
  const keyIdx = header.indexOf(CFG.KEY_HEADER);
  if (keyIdx === -1) throw new Error('Header "' + CFG.KEY_HEADER + '" not found in CSV');

  // Strip the ID_ prefix. Cells are formatted as text below, so digits stay intact.
  const prefIdx = header.indexOf(CFG.PREFIXED_HEADER);
  const data = rows.slice(1).filter(r => r.length === numCols && String(r[keyIdx]).trim() !== '');
  if (prefIdx !== -1) {
    data.forEach(r => {
      const v = String(r[prefIdx] || '');
      if (v.indexOf(CFG.PREFIX) === 0) r[prefIdx] = v.substring(CFG.PREFIX.length);
    });
  }

  // De-duplicate within the file (last row wins)
  const incoming = new Map();
  data.forEach(r => incoming.set(String(r[keyIdx]).trim(), r));

  // Sheet empty -> write header + everything
  const lastRow = sheet.getLastRow();
  if (lastRow < 1) {
    setTextFormats_(sheet, header, 2, incoming.size + 1);
    const out = [header].concat(Array.from(incoming.values()));
    sheet.getRange(1, 1, out.length, numCols).setValues(out);
    return { updated: 0, appended: incoming.size };
  }

  // Safety: sheet header must match the CSV header
  const sheetHeader = sheet.getRange(1, 1, 1, numCols).getValues()[0].map(h => String(h).trim());
  if (sheetHeader.join('|') !== header.join('|')) {
    throw new Error('Sheet header differs from CSV header. Fix the sheet or the query before loading.\nSheet: ' +
      sheetHeader.join(',') + '\nCSV: ' + header.join(','));
  }

  // Read existing rows, overwrite matches in memory, collect new ones
  const existing = lastRow > 1 ? sheet.getRange(2, 1, lastRow - 1, numCols).getValues() : [];
  const rowOf = new Map();
  existing.forEach((r, i) => rowOf.set(String(r[keyIdx]).trim(), i));

  const toAppend = [];
  let updated = 0;
  incoming.forEach((r, key) => {
    const i = rowOf.get(key);
    if (i === undefined) toAppend.push(r);
    else { existing[i] = r; updated++; }
  });

  const newLast = lastRow + toAppend.length;
  setTextFormats_(sheet, header, 2, newLast);     // before writing, so long IDs stay text

  if (existing.length) sheet.getRange(2, 1, existing.length, numCols).setValues(existing);
  if (toAppend.length) sheet.getRange(lastRow + 1, 1, toAppend.length, numCols).setValues(toAppend);

  return { updated: updated, appended: toAppend.length };
}

function setTextFormats_(sheet, header, firstRow, lastRow) {
  if (lastRow < firstRow) return;
  CFG.TEXT_HEADERS.forEach(name => {
    const idx = header.indexOf(name);
    if (idx !== -1) sheet.getRange(firstRow, idx + 1, lastRow - firstRow + 1, 1).setNumberFormat('@');
  });
}

/************************************************************
 * PI COMMERCE — SAFE MERCHANT INFORMATION SYNC
 *
 * Supports:
 * 1. Old sheet format
 * 2. New sheet format
 * 3. New format with an extra blank field
 *
 * Duplicate customer IDs are allowed.
 * The LAST occurrence in the sheet wins.
 *
 * Unknown/misaligned rows STOP the whole sync.
 *
 * Writes directly to Neon in batches of 2,000 (the old single
 * POST to Vercel hit Vercel's 4.5 MB limit -> 413 errors).
 * Needs script property: NEON_DATABASE_URL
 *
 * OUTLETS: every row's MID (the "PizzaW…"-style ID near column B)
 * is also saved with that row's merchant name in merchant_outlets,
 * so a merchant with several outlets under one customer ID shows
 * each outlet's own name on its onboarding case. A missing MID is
 * simply skipped; it never stops the sync.
 ************************************************************/


function normalizeCell(value) {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') {
    return null;
  }

  if (typeof value === 'number') {
    if (!isFinite(value)) return null;
    return String(Math.trunc(value));
  }

  var s = String(value).trim();
  return s || null;
}


function digitsOnly(value) {
  var s = normalizeCell(value);
  if (!s) return '';
  return String(s).replace(/\D/g, '');
}


function looksLikePhone(value) {
  var d = digitsOnly(value);

  return (
    d.length === 10 ||
    (d.length === 11 && d.charAt(0) === '0') ||
    (d.length === 12 && d.indexOf('91') === 0)
  );
}


function normalizePhone(value) {
  var d = digitsOnly(value);

  if (!d) return null;

  if (d.length === 11 && d.charAt(0) === '0') {
    d = d.substring(1);
  }

  if (d.length === 12 && d.indexOf('91') === 0) {
    d = d.substring(2);
  }

  return d || null;
}


function looksLikeCustomerId(value) {
  var s = normalizeCell(value);
  if (!s) return false;
  return /^\d{5,15}$/.test(s);
}


function looksLikeMcc(value) {
  var s = normalizeCell(value);
  if (!s) return false;
  // Source has valid 3-digit and 4-digit MCCs.
  return /^\d{3,4}$/.test(s);
}


/*
 * MID of a row: letters and digits mixed, 10+ characters (e.g. PizzaW75532028120279).
 * Looked for in column B first, then A and C.
 */
function findMid_(row) {
  var cols = [1, 0, 2];
  for (var i = 0; i < cols.length; i++) {
    var v = normalizeCell(row[cols[i]]);
    if (v && /^[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}$/.test(v) && /[A-Za-z]/.test(v) && /\d/.test(v)) return v;
  }
  return null;
}


/************************************************************
 * FINAL SAFETY CHECK
 ************************************************************/

function isMerchantRecordSafe(record) {
  if (!record) return false;

  if (!record.customer_id || !looksLikeCustomerId(record.customer_id)) {
    return false;
  }

  if (!record.merchant_name) {
    return false;
  }

  if (record.phone_number && !looksLikePhone(record.phone_number)) {
    return false;
  }

  // SMB is merchant type, never category.
  if (record.category && String(record.category).trim().toUpperCase() === 'SMB') {
    return false;
  }

  // Detect customer ID accidentally shifted into sub-category.
  if (record.sub_category && /^\d{5,15}$/.test(String(record.sub_category).trim())) {
    return false;
  }

  return true;
}


/************************************************************
 * DETECT THE THREE KNOWN SOURCE FORMATS
 ************************************************************/

function normalizeMerchantRow(row) {

  // Zero-based: D=3 E=4 F=5 G=6 H=7 I=8 J=9 K=10
  var d = normalizeCell(row[3]);
  var e = normalizeCell(row[4]);
  var f = normalizeCell(row[5]);
  var g = normalizeCell(row[6]);
  var h = normalizeCell(row[7]);
  var i = normalizeCell(row[8]);
  var j = normalizeCell(row[9]);
  var k = normalizeCell(row[10]);

  /***********************
   * FORMAT 1 — OLD
   * D merchant, E phone, F customer ID, G category,
   * H sub-category, I MCC, J SMB
   ***********************/
  if (
    looksLikePhone(e) &&
    looksLikeCustomerId(f) &&
    g &&
    h &&
    looksLikeMcc(i) &&
    String(j || '').toUpperCase() === 'SMB'
  ) {
    var oldRecord = {
      format: 'old',
      customer_id: normalizeCell(f),
      merchant_name: normalizeCell(d),
      phone_number: normalizePhone(e),
      category: normalizeCell(g),
      sub_category: normalizeCell(h)
    };
    return isMerchantRecordSafe(oldRecord) ? oldRecord : null;
  }

  /***********************
   * FORMAT 2 — NEW
   * D merchant, E display name, F phone, G SMB,
   * H customer ID, I category, J sub-category
   ***********************/
  if (
    looksLikePhone(f) &&
    String(g || '').toUpperCase() === 'SMB' &&
    looksLikeCustomerId(h) &&
    i &&
    j
  ) {
    var newRecord = {
      format: 'new',
      customer_id: normalizeCell(h),
      merchant_name: normalizeCell(d),
      phone_number: normalizePhone(f),
      category: normalizeCell(i),
      sub_category: normalizeCell(j)
    };
    return isMerchantRecordSafe(newRecord) ? newRecord : null;
  }

  /***********************
   * FORMAT 3 — NEW + BLANK
   * D merchant, E display name, F blank, G phone, H SMB,
   * I customer ID, J category, K sub-category
   ***********************/
  if (
    !f &&
    looksLikePhone(g) &&
    String(h || '').toUpperCase() === 'SMB' &&
    looksLikeCustomerId(i) &&
    j &&
    k
  ) {
    var shiftedRecord = {
      format: 'new_shifted',
      customer_id: normalizeCell(i),
      merchant_name: normalizeCell(d),
      phone_number: normalizePhone(g),
      category: normalizeCell(j),
      sub_category: normalizeCell(k)
    };
    return isMerchantRecordSafe(shiftedRecord) ? shiftedRecord : null;
  }

  // Unknown structure = never guess.
  return null;
}


/************************************************************
 * BUILD COMPLETE SAFE PAYLOAD
 ************************************************************/

function buildMerchantRows() {

  var spreadsheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  var sheet = spreadsheet.getSheetByName('Onboardings');

  if (!sheet) {
    throw new Error('Sheet named "Onboardings" not found.');
  }

  var values = sheet.getDataRange().getDisplayValues();

  if (values.length < 2) {
    throw new Error('No merchant rows found in Onboardings.');
  }

  // Keyed by customer ID: a later duplicate replaces an earlier one.
  var byCustomer = {};
  var customerOrder = [];
  var badRows = [];
  // Keyed by MID: each outlet's own name (one customer ID can have many MIDs).
  var byMid = {};

  var oldCount = 0;
  var newCount = 0;
  var shiftedNewCount = 0;
  var duplicateCount = 0;

  for (var r = 1; r < values.length; r++) {

    var sheetRowNumber = r + 1;
    var sourceRow = values[r];

    var allBlank = sourceRow.every(function(value) {
      return String(value || '').trim() === '';
    });

    if (allBlank) {
      continue;
    }

    var merchant = normalizeMerchantRow(sourceRow);

    if (!merchant) {
      badRows.push(sheetRowNumber);
      continue;
    }

    if (byCustomer[merchant.customer_id]) {
      duplicateCount++;
    } else {
      customerOrder.push(merchant.customer_id);
    }

    // IMPORTANT: last occurrence wins.
    byCustomer[merchant.customer_id] = {
      customer_id: merchant.customer_id,
      merchant_name: merchant.merchant_name,
      phone_number: merchant.phone_number,
      category: merchant.category,
      sub_category: merchant.sub_category
    };

    var mid = findMid_(sourceRow);
    if (mid) {
      byMid[mid] = { mid: mid, customer_id: merchant.customer_id, merchant_name: merchant.merchant_name };
    }

    if (merchant.format === 'old') oldCount++;
    if (merchant.format === 'new') newCount++;
    if (merchant.format === 'new_shifted') shiftedNewCount++;
  }

  /***********************
   * SAFETY STOP
   ***********************/
  if (badRows.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(
      'SYNC STOPPED. ' + badRows.length +
      ' populated rows have an unknown or misaligned structure. ' +
      'Nothing was sent to Neon. ' +
      'Example sheet rows: ' + badRows.slice(0, 25).join(', ')
    );
  }

  var rows = customerOrder.map(function(customerId) {
    return byCustomer[customerId];
  });

  if (rows.length < 100) {
    throw new Error(
      'SYNC STOPPED. Only ' + rows.length +
      ' unique valid merchants were found. Nothing was sent to Neon.'
    );
  }

  return {
    rows: rows,
    outlets: Object.keys(byMid).map(function(m) { return byMid[m]; }),
    oldCount: oldCount,
    newCount: newCount,
    shiftedNewCount: shiftedNewCount,
    duplicateCount: duplicateCount
  };
}


/************************************************************
 * SAFETY CUSTOMER CHECK
 ************************************************************/

function findSafetyCustomer_(rows) {
  for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
    if (String(rows[i].customer_id) === '1278049194') {
      return rows[i];
    }
  }
  return null;
}


function safetyCustomerIsCorrect_(c) {
  return !!c &&
    c.customer_id === '1278049194' &&

    c.sub_category === 'IOCL Pump';
}


/************************************************************
 * SAFE PREVIEW — DOES NOT WRITE TO NEON
 ************************************************************/

function previewMerchantInformationSync() {

  var result = buildMerchantRows();

  console.log('==============================');
  console.log('MERCHANT SYNC PREVIEW SUCCESS');
  console.log('==============================');
  console.log('Unique merchants to sync: ' + result.rows.length);
  console.log('Duplicate source rows safely deduplicated: ' + result.duplicateCount);
  console.log('Old-format rows: ' + result.oldCount);
  console.log('New-format rows: ' + result.newCount);
  console.log('Shifted-new rows: ' + result.shiftedNewCount);
  console.log('Outlets (MIDs) found: ' + result.outlets.length);
  console.log('Pizza Wings outlets: ' + JSON.stringify(result.outlets.filter(function(o) { return o.customer_id === '1003024598'; })));

  var testCustomer = findSafetyCustomer_(result.rows);

  console.log('CHECK CUSTOMER 1278049194');
  console.log(JSON.stringify(testCustomer));

  if (!safetyCustomerIsCorrect_(testCustomer)) {
    throw new Error(
      'Preview failed: customer 1278049194 does not map correctly. ' +
      'DO NOT RUN LIVE SYNC.'
    );
  }

  console.log('TEST CUSTOMER IS CORRECT.');
  console.log('PREVIEW PASSED.');
  console.log('NO DATA WAS SENT TO NEON.');
}


/************************************************************
 * NEON CONNECTION
 ************************************************************/

var SYNC_BATCH_SIZE = 2000;

// Stop if the sheet suddenly has 10%+ fewer merchants than the
// last successful sync (protects against a half-pasted sheet).
var MAX_DROP_RATIO = 0.10;


function getNeonUrl_() {
  var cs = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty('NEON_DATABASE_URL');
  if (!cs) {
    throw new Error('Missing script property NEON_DATABASE_URL.');
  }
  return cs.trim();
}


/*
 * Runs SQL over Neon's HTTPS endpoint.
 * body = { query, params }              -> one statement
 * body = { queries: [{query, params}] } -> one transaction
 */
function neonSql_(connectionString, body) {
  var afterAt = connectionString.substring(connectionString.lastIndexOf('@') + 1);
  var host = afterAt.split('/')[0].split('?')[0];

  var headers = {
    'Neon-Connection-String': connectionString,
    'Neon-Raw-Text-Output': 'true',
    'Neon-Array-Mode': 'true'
  };

  if (body.queries) {
    headers['Neon-Batch-Isolation-Level'] = 'ReadCommitted';
  }

  var response = UrlFetchApp.fetch('https://' + host + '/sql', {
    method: 'post',
    contentType: 'application/json',
    headers: headers,
    payload: JSON.stringify(body),
    muteHttpExceptions: true
  });

  var code = response.getResponseCode();
  var text = response.getContentText();

  if (code < 200 || code >= 300) {
    throw new Error('Neon query failed (' + code + '): ' + text.slice(0, 500));
  }

  return JSON.parse(text);
}


/************************************************************
 * READ-ONLY CONNECTION TEST
 ************************************************************/

function testNeonConnection() {
  var res = neonSql_(getNeonUrl_(), {
    query:
      'SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE active), ' +
      'max(last_synced_at)::text FROM merchant_information',
    params: []
  });

  var r = res.rows[0];
  console.log('Connected to Neon.');
  console.log('merchant_information total: ' + r[0] +
              ', active: ' + r[1] +
              ', last sync: ' + r[2]);
}


/************************************************************
 * LIVE FULL SYNC
 ************************************************************/

var UPSERT_SQL =
  'INSERT INTO merchant_information ' +
  '(customer_id, merchant_name, phone_number, category, sub_category, active, last_synced_at) ' +
  'SELECT r.customer_id, r.merchant_name, r.phone_number, r.category, r.sub_category, ' +
  'true, $2::timestamptz ' +
  'FROM json_to_recordset($1::json) AS r(' +
  'customer_id text, merchant_name text, phone_number text, category text, sub_category text) ' +
  'ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET ' +
  'merchant_name = EXCLUDED.merchant_name, ' +
  'phone_number = EXCLUDED.phone_number, ' +
  'category = EXCLUDED.category, ' +
  'sub_category = EXCLUDED.sub_category, ' +
  'active = true, ' +
  'last_synced_at = EXCLUDED.last_synced_at';

var OUTLETS_SQL =
  'INSERT INTO merchant_outlets (mid, customer_id, merchant_name, synced_at) ' +
  'SELECT r.mid, r.customer_id, r.merchant_name, now() ' +
  'FROM json_to_recordset($1::json) AS r(mid text, customer_id text, merchant_name text) ' +
  'ON CONFLICT (mid) DO UPDATE SET ' +
  'customer_id = EXCLUDED.customer_id, ' +
  'merchant_name = EXCLUDED.merchant_name, ' +
  'synced_at = now()';


function syncMerchantInformation() {
  var cs = getNeonUrl_();

  var result = buildMerchantRows();
  var rows = result.rows;

  if (!safetyCustomerIsCorrect_(findSafetyCustomer_(rows))) {
    throw new Error(
      'LIVE SYNC STOPPED. Safety customer 1278049194 does not map correctly. ' +
      'Nothing was sent to Neon.'
    );
  }

  var sourceName = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getName() + ' / Onboardings';

  // Drop guard
  var last = neonSql_(cs, {
    query:
      "SELECT row_count FROM merchant_sync_runs " +
      "WHERE status = 'success' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1",
    params: []
  });

  if (last.rows.length) {
    var lastCount = parseInt(last.rows[0][0], 10);
    if (rows.length < lastCount * (1 - MAX_DROP_RATIO)) {
      throw new Error(
        'SYNC STOPPED. Sheet has ' + rows.length + ' merchants vs ' + lastCount +
        ' in the last sync. Nothing was sent to Neon.'
      );
    }
  }

  // Upsert in batches
  var runStart = new Date().toISOString();
  var batches = Math.ceil(rows.length / SYNC_BATCH_SIZE);

  console.log('Sending ' + rows.length + ' unique validated merchants in ' +
              batches + ' batches...');

  for (var b = 0; b < batches; b++) {
    var chunk = rows.slice(b * SYNC_BATCH_SIZE, (b + 1) * SYNC_BATCH_SIZE);

    neonSql_(cs, {
      query: UPSERT_SQL,
      params: [JSON.stringify(chunk), runStart]
    });

    console.log('Batch ' + (b + 1) + '/' + batches + ' done (' + chunk.length + ').');
  }

  // Verify every merchant was written before deactivating anyone
  var check = neonSql_(cs, {
    query: 'SELECT count(*) FROM merchant_information WHERE last_synced_at = $1::timestamptz',
    params: [runStart]
  });

  var written = parseInt(check.rows[0][0], 10);

  if (written !== rows.length) {
    throw new Error(
      'SYNC STOPPED BEFORE DEACTIVATION. Expected ' + rows.length +
      ', found ' + written + '. No merchants were deactivated. Run again.'
    );
  }

  // Deactivate merchants no longer in the sheet + log the run (one transaction)
  var finalRes = neonSql_(cs, {
    queries: [
      {
        query:
          'UPDATE merchant_information SET active = false ' +
          'WHERE active AND last_synced_at < $1::timestamptz',
        params: [runStart]
      },
      {
        query:
          'INSERT INTO merchant_sync_runs ' +
          '(started_at, completed_at, row_count, source_name, status) ' +
          "VALUES ($1::timestamptz, now(), $2::int, $3, 'success')",
        params: [runStart, rows.length, sourceName]
      }
    ]
  });

  var deactivated =
    (finalRes.results && finalRes.results[0] && finalRes.results[0].rowCount) || 0;

  // Outlet names per MID. Never stops the merchant sync if it fails.
  var outletsSaved = 0;
  try {
    var outlets = result.outlets;
    for (var o = 0; o < outlets.length; o += SYNC_BATCH_SIZE) {
      var part = outlets.slice(o, o + SYNC_BATCH_SIZE);
      neonSql_(cs, { query: OUTLETS_SQL, params: [JSON.stringify(part)] });
      outletsSaved += part.length;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.log('Outlet names not saved (merchant sync itself succeeded): ' + err);
  }

  console.log('==============================');
  console.log('MERCHANT SYNC SUCCESS');
  console.log('Upserted ' + rows.length + ' unique merchants.');
  console.log('Marked inactive (no longer in sheet): ' + deactivated);
  console.log('Duplicate sheet rows deduplicated: ' + result.duplicateCount);
  console.log('Outlet names saved (by MID): ' + outletsSaved);
  console.log('==============================');
}


/************************************************************
 * NIGHTLY TRIGGER
 ************************************************************/

function createNightlyTrigger() {

  ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers().forEach(function(trigger) {
    if (trigger.getHandlerFunction() === 'syncMerchantInformation') {
      ScriptApp.deleteTrigger(trigger);
    }
  });

  ScriptApp
    .newTrigger('syncMerchantInformation')
    .timeBased()
    .atHour(2)
    .nearMinute(30)
    .everyDays(1)
    .create();

  console.log('Nightly merchant sync trigger created.');
}

 *
 * Paste into the "Onboardings_Updated_List" sheet: Extensions → Apps Script. Then:
 *   1. Project Settings → Script Properties → add
 *        PI_COMMERCE_AD_CONVERSIONS_SYNC_URL  https://pi-commerce-call-center-disposition.vercel.app/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync
 *        PI_COMMERCE_SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET      (the same secret the Sub Raw / CSM syncs use)
 *   2. Run setupAdConversionsTrigger once (approve the permissions). It sends the tab now and then
 *      every day at about 9:40 AM, alongside the CSM sync (set the Apps Script time zone to
 *      Asia/Kolkata in Project Settings). Run syncAdConversions any time to push the latest numbers.
 *
 * Reads, by header name, CustID, Ad_ID (the Ads ID — not Meta_AD_ID), Ad_Creative_Name and
 * Conversations from the "New" tab. The portal matches each ad on Ad_ID = AdsRun Raw "Ads ID".
 */
const ADCONV_SHEET = 'New';
const ADCONV_BATCH = 1000;

function setupAdConversionsTrigger() {
  ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers()
    .filter(t => t.getHandlerFunction() === 'syncAdConversions')
    .forEach(t => ScriptApp.deleteTrigger(t));
  ScriptApp.newTrigger('syncAdConversions').timeBased().everyDays(1).atHour(9).nearMinute(40).create();
  syncAdConversions();
}

function syncAdConversions() {
  const props = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties();
  const url = props.getProperty('PI_COMMERCE_AD_CONVERSIONS_SYNC_URL');
  const [redacted]
  if (!url || !secret) throw new Error('Set PI_COMMERCE_AD_CONVERSIONS_SYNC_URL and PI_COMMERCE_SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET in Script Properties');
  const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getSheetByName(ADCONV_SHEET);
  if (!sheet) throw new Error('Tab "' + ADCONV_SHEET + '" not found');
  const values = sheet.getDataRange().getDisplayValues();
  // "Ad_ID" / "Ad ID" / "ad_id" all match; Meta_AD_ID is a different column and is not used.
  const header = values[0].map(h => String(h).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, '_'));
  const col = names => { for (const n of names) { const i = header.indexOf(n); if (i >= 0) return i; } return -1; };
  const c = { cust: col(['custid', 'customer_id']), ad: col(['ad_id']), name: col(['ad_creative_name', 'ad_name']), conv: col(['conversations']) };
  if (c.cust < 0 || c.ad < 0 || c.conv < 0) throw new Error('Missing CustID / Ad_ID / Conversations headers');
  const rows = [];
  for (let r = 1; r < values.length; r++) {
    const v = values[r];
    if (!v[c.cust] || !v[c.ad]) continue;
    rows.push({ customer_id: v[c.cust], ad_id: v[c.ad], ad_name: c.name >= 0 ? v[c.name] : '', conversions: v[c.conv] });
  }
  let saved = 0, skipped = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < rows.length; i += ADCONV_BATCH) {
    const res = UrlFetchApp.fetch(url, {
      method: 'post', contentType: 'application/json', muteHttpExceptions: true,
      headers: { 'x-sub-raw-sync-secret': secret },
      payload: JSON.stringify({ rows: rows.slice(i, i + ADCONV_BATCH) })
    });
    if (res.getResponseCode() !== 200) throw new Error('Portal said ' + res.getResponseCode() + ': ' + res.getContentText().slice(0, 300));
    const j = JSON.parse(res.getContentText()); saved += j.saved || 0; skipped += j.skipped || 0;
  }
  console.log('Ad conversions sync: ' + rows.length + ' rows, saved ' + saved + ', skipped ' + skipped);
}
